Metformin XR BE Safe Space — IR High-Variability Sensitivity (PBPK)

Reference T50 = 3.0 h · within-subject CV = immediate-release (Cmax 23.7%, AUC 14.7%)

Author

Nikita

Published

June 9, 2026

Purpose

This is a sensitivity companion to the main report (be_safe_space_report.html). It repeats the virtual-bioequivalence (VBE) safe-space analysis — same PBPK population, same 3.0 h reference, same 500 trials at n = 48 and 86 — but substitutes the higher within-subject variability of metformin IMMEDIATE-release for the extended-release values. The question: how much does the safe space shrink if the product behaved like a higher-variability formulation?

Metformin is a low-variability drug, but reported intra-subject CVs span a range. The IR / upper-bound values used here bracket that range:

The point average-BE estimates (GMR and 90% CI) are unchanged from the main report — they are deterministic and do not depend on the assumed within-subject CV. Only the VBE power (and hence the safe-space width) changes. See the main report for the BE table.

Safe space by endpoint (IR variability; 500 trials; n = 48 and 86)

Green = safe space (power ≥ 80%), red = fail; open circles = the 8 simulated formulations; a tick marks every simulated T50.

Cmax (BE-determining endpoint)

Inference. Under IR variability the Cmax safe space narrows sharply to 2.30–3.75 h (n=48) / 2.10–3.90 h (n=86) — versus 2.00–4.15 / 1.80–4.25 h under ER. Higher trial noise widens the 90% CI, so formulations farther from the reference can no longer pass reliably.

AUC0-t

Inference. AUC0-t stays comparatively wide (~1.0–4.4/4.55 h): its lower assumed CV (14.7%) and smaller true exposure change with release rate keep power high except at the slow extreme. It does not limit the joint decision.

AUC∞

Inference. As in the main report, AUC∞ is not reliable for the slow arms (extrapolation artefact) and should not drive the XR safe space.

Joint decision (Cmax & AUC0-t)

Inference. The regulatory (joint) safe space contracts to ≈ 2.30–3.70 h (n=48) / 2.15–3.90 h (n=86), again governed by Cmax.

ER vs IR safe-space comparison

Inference. Type I error remains controlled (≤ 5%) at the truly non-equivalent slow arms even under higher variability. The cost of higher CV is lost power near the edges, which is what contracts the safe space — not an increase in false-positive BE.

Conclusion

Raising within-subject variability from ER (~12%) to IR/high (~24% Cmax) narrows the joint safe space by roughly 0.4–0.5 h on each side (≈1.95–4.10 h → ≈2.30–3.70 h at n=48). The qualitative findings are unchanged: Cmax is limiting, AUC₀-t is permissive, AUC∞ is artefactual, and Type I error stays controlled. A higher-variability product therefore demands a tighter formulation T50 tolerance to remain bioequivalent to the 3.0 h reference.
